# Limitations {#sec-limitations}

**The metric comparisons are out of sample; the model underneath them is
not.** The model was selected with knowledge of these test races across five
papers: features, objective, function class, encoder architecture and the rung
ladder were each chosen after seeing earlier papers' test results. Paper 6
fits nothing, so the comparisons in @sec-roi and @sec-p2 are out of sample as
comparisons. The models being compared are not.

**@sec-beta is measured against a forecast price, not a traded one.** The
coefficient describes how much of the model's disagreement with a compiler's
published estimate the market later accepts. No early traded price appears
anywhere in this dataset, so the corresponding figure against one cannot be
measured here.

**The thin bins below 0.10 carry small win counts.** The bottom bin holds
`r p6m_n(min(p6m_p2_bins$wins[p6m_p2_bins$bin == "0-2%"]))` to
`r p6m_n(max(p6m_p2_bins$wins[p6m_p2_bins$bin == "0-2%"]))` winners depending
on the source, and one bin has too few rows to support an interval at all.
Counts sit beside every score in @sec-p2 for that reason.
